headline: Gulf Coast Shelling and Mangrove Preserve Access
reservation: Entrance to J.N. 'Ding' Darling National Wildlife Refuge is managed by the federal government and is separate from Sanibel Causeway tolls. Many local beach parking lots use mobile payment apps; travelers should check the official city website for current parking hourly rates. Peak season lodging requires months of lead time for both Sanibel and Captiva.

days.title: River District and Invention

stops.name: Edison and Ford Winter Estates
stops.detail: Tour the historic laboratory, botanical gardens, and winter homes of Thomas Edison and Henry Ford.

stops.name: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve
stops.detail: Walk the 1.2-mile boardwalk through a wetland ecosystem to spot local wading birds and alligators.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers; urban traffic can be heavy during midday
days.note: Insect repellent is recommended for the shaded boardwalk areas year-round.

days.title: Sanibel Island Immersion

stops.name: J.N. 'Ding' Darling National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Drive or cycle Wildlife Drive to observe migratory birds and manatees in the mangrove estuaries.

stops.name: Bowman's Beach
stops.detail: Visit this remote stretch of sand for renowned shelling opportunities away from the main resort areas.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; the Sanibel Causeway can experience significant backups
days.note: Wildlife Drive is closed to vehicles on Fridays; plan your visit accordingly.

days.title: Captiva and Coastal Waters

stops.name: Turner Beach
stops.detail: Stop at the Blind Pass bridge area for a view of the channel between Sanibel and Captiva.

stops.name: Captiva Village
stops.detail: Explore the narrow, sandy lanes of the village on foot to see the unique coastal architecture.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the slow-paced island drive; parking is very limited on Captiva
days.note: Check local tide charts if planning to shell, as low tide offers the best results.

intel.title: Sanibel Lot Management
intel.text: Beach parking lots on Sanibel are limited and fill early in the winter season. Most lots require a fee paid via a central kiosk or mobile application.

intel.title: Causeway Transit
intel.text: The Sanibel Causeway is the only road access to the islands and requires a toll. Check the official Lee County DOT site for current transponder requirements.

intel.title: Island Supply Limits
intel.text: Fuel stations are located on Sanibel but are absent on Captiva. Fill your tank in Fort Myers or near the causeway entrance to ensure coverage.

intel.title: Wildlife Drive Hours
intel.text: Refuge hours vary by sunset times; the gates close promptly. Always confirm the current week's schedule at the visitor center before entering the loop.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Reception is strong in downtown Fort Myers but can be intermittent in the dense mangroves of the wildlife refuge. Use physical maps for navigating the northern end of Captiva.

plan.arrival: Arrive at RSW, pick up your rental, and head to the McGregor Boulevard area for grocery supplies before crossing to the islands.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for most areas, but a convertible or Jeep is popular for island sightseeing; check for height restrictions in parking garages.
plan.goldenHour: The Sanibel Causeway bridge offers a wide perspective of the sunset over the Gulf of Mexico, though stopping on the bridge is prohibited.
